prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: B009 as a single part, with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After reading all eight statements, the scientific case still rests on the same points. Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state, which gave a new classification of band insulators without any broken symmetry. Molenkamp's group then observed the predicted protected edge transport in HgTe quantum wells. The result has been reproduced in other materials and by transport, ARPES and STM over about two decades, so both its maturity and its interpretation are settled. I want to be explicit that this is my judgment of the physics and not a reaction to the six-to-two count the chair reports. The question that decides it for me is credit. B009 is the only shortlisted candidate where a three-name theory-plus-experiment split follows the actual logic of the discovery, even though it leaves out real claimants. On novelty against 2016, my answer to the chair is that the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and topological phases in model systems, in the Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz setting. The B009 step is different. It shows that ordinary band insulators carry a Z2 topological invariant and that this is observable in a real material with protected edge conduction. The citation should say this and should name the quantum spin Hall state and HgTe explicitly, so it does not read as a general prize for topology. I accept the narrower two-dimensional framing, and I would rather state it openly than write a broad citation that implies credit the trio cannot carry.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real and I do not think the committee should hide it. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal identified HgTe and was the trigger for Molenkamp's experiment. Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES work is a separate and major step. Neither fits inside a three-name limit built on the supplied names. If the committee prefers to treat the 2D and 3D steps as one discovery, then Hasan or a different third name would be needed and the present trio would be wrong. I also take Kroll's point that some will see this as a follow-on to 2016 and that its novelty is partly spent. I judge the difference described above to be sufficient, but it is a judgment call and members who disagree are not being unreasonable. I do not claim that B009 is uncontested, only that its weaknesses are better understood, and more openly statable in a citation, than those of the alternatives.

responses.point: Kroll holds that B026 is the cleanest credit on the shortlist, but that the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes and the unverified magic-wavelength priority are the main risk, and that B009's novelty is partly spent after 2016.
responses.response: I agree with you that the Katori-Ye credit boundary is cleaner than anything in B009, and I do not want to understate that. Where we differ is on what the cleaner boundary is worth. The two weaknesses you list for B026, the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and the priority question that neither you nor Lindroth can check from the materials, are about whether it is a distinct discovery at all. B009's weakness is about which names to attach to a discovery that every member who discussed it accepts as real. I would rather resolve a naming problem than a separability problem. On novelty, my reply is above: 2016 covered topological phase transitions and phases, while B009 is the realisation of a Z2 band invariant in a real insulator. If B026 were the committee's choice I would not object, and I keep it as my first alternative. I do not think that a clean credit alone outweighs a doubt about separability from earlier prizes.

responses.point: Pearce asks whether the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits makes B010 ineligible this year or only a timing question, and whether I should recuse.
responses.response: I see it as a timing and attribution question, not a disqualification. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in a circuit, while circuit QED concerns strong coupling of an artificial atom to a resonator and the processor architecture that followed, so the discoveries are separable. But awarding a neighbouring superconducting-circuit theme straight after 2025 is hard to defend, and the attribution among Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf, with Girvin outside the names, is not settled. That is why I am not asking the committee to consider B010 this year. On recusal: I would recuse myself from any deliberation that sets B010 against another candidate, and I am not including it as an alternative here for that reason. I also thank you for moving to B009 on the merits of the credit argument rather than on count alone.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that B037 should be an experimental trio of Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger, and that B026 is a distinct discovery with a clean two-name credit that makes B009's wider support not the committee's centre of gravity.
responses.response: I accept your warning that a count is not the committee's centre of gravity, and I have tried to argue for B009 without leaning on it. On B037 I still think an experiment-only trio omits the theoretical origin in Jaksch and Zoller, and a theory-inclusive version leaves out Esslinger and ties this to B030 through Zoller and Cirac. That is a larger credit problem than the one in B009, which is why I list B037 only as a second alternative. On your point that lattice clocks are distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, I find the argument plausible, but the magic-wavelength priority rests on recollection, and I would want the committee to confirm it before relying on it. If B026 is the position that carries the committee after this discussion, I could support it.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps Mele in the B009 trio but treats Hasan's 3D work as a possible different, larger prize, and favours a narrow citation around the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on how the third slot should be justified. I would go slightly further on the citation. A narrow wording around the quantum spin Hall state and its HgTe realisation does not erase Hasan or the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. It states the achievement for which these three names are responsible. If the committee later regards the 3D step as a separate prize, that remains open. Your point that the Z2 invariant underlies both the HgTe result and the 3D classification is the main reason I think Mele, and not Hasan, is the defensible third name here. Where I part from the narrowest wording is that I would keep the phrase about first experimental realisation, since the prediction-then-observation structure is what separates this prize from a general topology prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the 2D quantum spin Hall step as a complete achievement without Hasan and without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, or whether it will treat 2D and 3D as one discovery requiring different names.
Whether the difference I draw from the 2016 prize, a Z2 band invariant realised in a real insulator versus topological phases in model systems, will be shared by members who see this as incremental.
The magic-wavelength priority and the claims of other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups for B026 are unverified from the supplied materials, and my view of that candidate depends on them.
My historical attributions for B009 rest on recollection and have not been checked against documents in this record.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: I am a professor at Chalmers and director of WACQT, working on circuit and waveguide QED and superconducting quantum computing, and my Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson work in the same area. I ranked B010 first in the opening ballot. I have dropped B010 from my preferred configuration and from my alternatives, and I would recuse myself from any deliberation that sets B010 against another candidate. I have no apparent connection to the credited names in B009, B026 or B037 from my profile.
